title: Research Request → Multi-Agent Crew → Cited Brief

sections.label: 1 · REQUEST
sections.note: A research question comes in from a form or Slack and is turned into a plan — the sub-questions that actually need answering before the main one can be.

sections.label: 2 · AGENT CREW
sections.note: A lead agent works the plan with real tools: web search, the internal document store, and a data lookup. Each sub-question is researched independently rather than answered from one long prompt.

sections.label: 3 · VERIFY
sections.note: A separate reviewer agent checks every claim against the sources actually retrieved and strips anything unsupported. The writer and the fact-checker being the same model in one pass is where these systems usually fail.

sections.label: 4 · DELIVER
sections.note: The verified brief is written to a doc with inline citations and posted back to the requester, with the full source list attached so any claim can be traced in one click.

input_sample.question: Should we build native Spanish-language support before expanding into Mexico, or is English-only viable for the first year?
input_sample.context: B2B SaaS, current customers are US mid-market logistics firms. Considering a Mexico City pilot in Q1.

output_sample.question: Should we build native Spanish-language support before expanding into Mexico?
output_sample.recommendation: English-only is viable for a Q1 pilot but not for scale. Mid-market Mexican logistics firms show high English proficiency at the decision-maker level, so the pilot can land without localization — but support tickets and end-user adoption are where English-only breaks down, and that surfaces around month four.

key_findings.finding: Decision-makers at target-size firms are predominantly English-comfortable
End-user adoption drops sharply without localized UI in this segment
Localization effort estimated at 6-9 weeks for UI plus ongoing support staffing
